grades.reason: The verbose lines log only cookie attributes (domain, path, secure, sameSite, httpOnly) — never the session id or cookie value — so nothing sensitive is exposed, and the tiered-logging pattern with a default of `light` matches every other lib in `server/src`.

The test does compare `domain` (it loops over `['path','httponly','samesite','domain','secure']` against the login cookie); the domain comparison is merely vacuous under `NODE_ENV=test` where no domain is set, which the test comment states explicitly and `tests/unit/sessionCookie.test.js` covers non-vacuously via a real Express round-trip with `SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN` set.

summary: Both local findings are false positives — one flags harmless attribute logging as a secret leak, the other claims an absent domain assertion that is in fact present and covered non-vacuously in the unit tests — and the review found nothing about the actual change.
